original_question: In mushroom billiards and related systems with mixed phase space, how does the boundary between regular and chaotic regions affect escape, including the slowing of survival decay caused by stickiness from marginally unstable periodic orbits and by the regular-chaotic interface itself?
target_in_paper: Section 11.4 ("Open billiards"), Mixed billiards subsection, Problem 11.11: "Characterise the escape properties of the boundary between regular and chaotic regions in mushroom and similar billiards."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the mixed-phase-space setting, the specific role of mushroom billiards, the regular/chaotic boundary as the object of study, and the two slowdown mechanisms named in the paper’s local context: stickiness from embedded marginally unstable periodic orbits and slowing caused by the interface itself.
missing_details: The paper’s exact target is not a broad question about mixed-phase-space systems in general, but the specific open problem about the boundary between regular and chaotic regions in mushroom and similar billiards.
The local context makes the question one about an open billiard with a hole H and survival probability P(t)=μ0(Ωt), where Ωt is the set of phase points that have not yet hit the hole by time t.
Section 11.4 takes μ0 to be, by default, the equilibrium measure for the billiard flow or the Poincaré map; your draft leaves that setup implicit.
The slowdown statement in the paper is made specifically for the case when the hole is placed in the chaotic region.
The paper emphasizes that the regular/chaotic boundary in mushroom billiards is smooth; this is part of why these billiards are singled out from more generic mixed systems.

The official formulation asks to characterize the escape properties of that boundary in general, not only the asymptotic survival-decay law; survival decay is the motivating manifestation discussed immediately beforehand.
No algebraic data such as ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or large-m quantifiers are relevant here; the missing specifications are geometric and dynamical instead.
refined_question: In the usual continuous-time open-billiard setting for the billiard flow, with Ωt={x∈Ω: Φs(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]} and survival probability P(t)=μ0(Ωt), consider a mushroom billiard, or a similar billiard whose phase space is mixed but whose regular and chaotic components are separated by a smooth boundary, and assume the hole H lies in the chaotic region. Characterize the escape properties associated with that regular-chaotic boundary; in particular, determine how the long-time survival/escape behaviour is affected, and possibly slowed, both by stickiness from embedded marginally unstable periodic orbits in the chaotic component and by the boundary/interface itself.
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Problem 11.11 rather than the broader Problem 11.10. In the mixed-billiards discussion, the paper first mentions the generic open problem of a universal decay rate, then narrows to mushroom billiards, highlighting their smooth regular-chaotic boundary and noting that, when the hole is in the chaotic region, survival may be slowed both by embedded marginally unstable periodic orbits and by the boundary itself. Those are exactly the cues reproduced in the draft, so the paper-faithful refinement is the specific boundary-escape problem of Problem 11.11.
